## 5. Leave-one-source-out

Major sources = at least 500 rows and both labels (8 of 11). Each fold trains on the train rows of every other source (same TF-IDF settings, vectorizer refit) and scores the held-out source's val+test rows. Clusters never straddle splits, so these rows have no >= 0.7 twin in the training rows. `in-dist F1` is the full model (section 4) on the same rows, so the difference is what losing the source costs. The last column scores all of the source's rows (train split too) for a steadier number on small sources; cross-source near-duplicates are not excluded there, so treat it as optimistic. Sources with one class (`cmu_hinglish_dog`, `hinglish_conversations`, `web_scams`) have no F1 and stay in training.

## 6. Attack rates in `augment.py`

Probabilities are per eligible character, so the share of characters actually changed in a message is lower (about p x the fraction of eligible letters). Only scam rows of at most 1000 characters are attacked. `random.seed(0)` is set once, so reruns are reproducible.

| attack | per-character probability | applies to | used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| homoglyph | 0.150 | each letter in the Cyrillic look-alike map (a e o p c x i y s) is swapped | train augmentation |
| leet | 0.200 | each letter in {a o i e s} becomes @ 0 1 3 $ | train augmentation |
| zero_width | 0.100 | a zero-width space is inserted after each letter | train augmentation |
| char_noise | 0.050 | each letter is swapped with its neighbour or deleted (50/50) | held-out test |
| url_obfuscate | n/a | every URL/domain token: http -> hxxp, '.' -> '[.]' | held-out test |
| spaced_keywords | n/a | every occurrence of KYC OTP UPI PIN account blocked verify lottery prize arrest is letter-spaced | held-out test |

## 7. Baseline TF-IDF n-grams

`baseline.py` uses **character** n-grams, not word n-grams: `analyzer="char_wb"` (character n-grams taken inside word boundaries, padded with spaces), `ngram_range=(2, 4)`, `min_df=3`, `max_features=200000`, `sublinear_tf=True`, text cut to the first 2000 characters, logistic regression with `class_weight=balanced`. Consequences: it needs no tokenizer, so Hindi and Kannada script work with the same code, and it tolerates the typo-style attacks better than word n-grams would, but it also picks up script, casing and boilerplate fragments that identify a source. A word-level run is the obvious ablation.
